title: Engine Ignition — Component Locations
introduction:
I read this transparent engine drawing as a map of the ignition system: match each callout to the adjacent Item and Description table, then look through the surrounding engine parts to see where the highlighted components sit. The transparency reveals their positions; it does not mean those parts are exposed on the assembled engine.

The ignition coil-on-plug is an electrical transformer positioned at its spark plug. It supplies the high voltage; the plug provides the controlled gap where the spark starts combustion. Think of the coil as the voltage elevator and the plug as the place that energy finally jumps the gap. The drawing shows their close relationship on both sides of the engine.

Use this reference to identify the components on the engine named below. Removal, plug selection, gap and tightening specifications require the applicable service information. Component location alone cannot identify the cause of a misfire; spark, fuel and the cylinder’s mechanical condition all matter.
